# NanoId

A Nano ID of the standard form: twenty-one characters from [`NanoIdAlphabet`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#nano-id-alphabet).

```rux
pub struct NanoId {
    // private fields
}
```

Copy, holding its text inline and owning nothing. Equality and ordering compare the text byte by byte.

## Associated functions

<h3 id="generate"><code>Generate</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Generate() -> NanoId ! EntropyError
```

A new identifier from the operating system's generator.
Costs twenty-one bytes of entropy and allocates nothing. Reports what the system reported when it could not
supply random bytes, and produces no identifier in that case.

**Returns**: the identifier, or why none could be made

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L57)

<h3 id="parse"><code>Parse</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Parse(text: char8[..]) -> NanoId ! NanoIdParseError
```

Reads a standard identifier from its text.
Reports `WrongLength` unless the text is exactly twenty-one bytes, and `InvalidCharacter` at the first byte
outside the default alphabet. A refused parse produces no value. Runs in constant time for a text of the
right length and allocates nothing.

| Name   | Type        | Description      |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the identifier, or why the text is not one

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L70)

## Methods

<h3 id="text"><code>Text</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Text(self: &NanoId) -> char8[..]
```

The identifier's twenty-one characters.
Borrows the value: the slice reads the value's own storage and must not outlive it. Cannot fail and
allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the text, always [`NanoIdLength`](/docs/api/nanoid/alphabet#nano-id-length) bytes of the default alphabet

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L89)

<h3 id="equals"><code>Equals</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Equals(self: &NanoId, other: &NanoId) -> bool
```

Whether two identifiers are the same.
Compares every byte whatever it finds, so the time taken does not reveal how much of a guessed identifier was
right. Cannot fail and allocates nothing.

| Name    | Type      | Description                       |
| ------- | --------- | --------------------------------- |
| `other` | `&NanoId` | the identifier to compare against |

**Returns**: whether the two have the same text

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L99)

<h3 id="compare"><code>Compare</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Compare(self: &NanoId, other: &NanoId) -> Ordering
```

The order of two identifiers' texts, byte by byte.
Identifiers are random, so this order means nothing beyond being total and stable, which is what a sorted
container needs. Cannot fail and allocates nothing.

| Name    | Type      | Description                       |
| ------- | --------- | --------------------------------- |
| `other` | `&NanoId` | the identifier to compare against |

**Returns**: how this identifier orders against `other`

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L115)

## Related

<h3 id="nano-id-parse-error"><code>NanoIdParseError</code></h3>

```rux
pub variant NanoIdParseError {
    WrongLength(uint),
    InvalidCharacter(uint)
}
```

Why text could not be read as a standard Nano ID.
Failure-only, carrying the zero-based byte offset where the problem was found. Copy, owning nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L23)

**Cases**

| Name                     | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WrongLength(uint)`      | The text is not twenty-one bytes long. The offset is the text's length when it is too short, and the first byte past the form when it is too long. |
| `InvalidCharacter(uint)` | A character that is not in the default alphabet. The offset is that character.                                                                     |

**Implements ParseFailure**

`NanoIdParseError` conforms to `ParseFailure`.

<h4 id="nano-id-parse-error-offset"><code>Offset</code></h4>

```rux
pub func Offset(self: &NanoIdParseError) -> uint
```

Where in the input the failure was found.
Borrows the error and leaves it untouched. Cannot fail; runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: the zero-based UTF-8 byte offset, which is the text's length at end of input

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/NanoId/Src/NanoId.rux#L36)
